principles.title: Autonomous by default; humans oversee the residual

decisionsOpen.trigger: Owen drafts; agent's next governance-cycle run
decisionsOpen.decisionForCEO: Decide which seats need real humans at licence-day (Board exec + NEDs, MLRO + FIC CO, IO, auditor, FAIS key individuals where applicable), who fills them, and how close to licence-grant they are appointed.

brief.summary: Banks Act + Companies Act + FIC + POPIA + FAIS together require a thin layer of real humans at licence-day. Owen drafts the composition (which seats, which humans, what cadence) for CEO approval. Replaces the prior 'when to start NED search' framing under the AI-driven-bank reframe.
brief.background: Under the AI-driven-bank operating model (2026-05-07), the bank's labour force is autonomous AI agents. Statutory humans are kept to the minimum the law requires. Realistically 5-10 humans at licence-day: Board exec + NEDs (Companies Act + Banks Act), CEO (Marc), MLRO + FIC Compliance Officer (FIC s.43A / s.43B), Information Officer (POPIA s.56), Auditor (Companies Act s.90 + Banks Act), and FAIS key individuals where Cat II/IIA mandate is sought. Marc currently covers CEO + interim Chair + interim IO + interim MLRO. Owen drafts which seats must have separate humans, candidate sourcing pathway, and timing relative to licence-application.

options.label: Marc covers maximum seats (interim)
options.description: Marc serves as CEO + Chair + IO + MLRO + FIC CO + interim director. NEDs + Auditor are the only additional humans.
options.consequence: Lowest human-headcount; concentrates fit-and-proper risk on Marc; SARB may push back on IO + MLRO concentration.

options.label: Marc + minimum independent layer
options.description: Marc covers CEO. NEDs (2-3) cover Chair + AC chair + RC chair. Separate IO, separate MLRO + FIC CO, separate Auditor.
options.consequence: 5-7 additional humans. SARB-credible; cleaner fit-and-proper distribution.

options.label: Standard SARB-licensed bank composition
options.description: Full Board (Chair + 3-4 NEDs + 1-2 EDs), separate CEO, CRO, CFO, CISO, IO, MLRO, FIC CO, Auditor, FAIS KIs.
options.consequence: 10-15 humans. Highest cost; safest licence-application posture; closest to a conventional bank.

options.label: Defer until SARB engagement
options.description: Hold the decision until external counsel (S5) advises on minimum composition.
options.consequence: Owen drafts alternatives; decision reopens after counsel engagement.

recommendation.stance: Marc + minimum independent layer.
recommendation.reasoning: SARB licence-application credibility requires independent IO and independent MLRO; Marc covering all four roles (CEO + IO + MLRO + Chair) concentrates fit-and-proper exposure and weakens the application. NEDs are required by Banks Act regardless. Going beyond the minimum independent layer is premature before counsel engages.

decisionsOpen.title: External legal counsel for SARB licence application
decisionsOpen.trigger: Imani recommends 2–3 firms with strengths-and-weaknesses notes

brief.summary: Major-firm external counsel is conventionally engaged 6–9 months ahead of SARB licence application. Imani recommends 2–3 firms with strengths-and-weaknesses notes.
brief.background:
Imani is the internal legal-as-code engineer; she runs ECTA execution, master-agreement-as-code, clause libraries, and the legal-entity tree. SARB licence applications conventionally engage a major-firm partner alongside internal counsel for: application drafting (long-form regulatory submissions), regulator engagement and meetings, licence-condition negotiation, and post-grant licence-condition compliance setup. Engagement timing is typically 6–9 months ahead of lodgment. Indicative licence lodgment from today is 12–18 months out, so the engagement decision can wait ~6 months but Imani's recommendation paper can land ahead of the engagement decision.

Under the AI-driven-bank reframe (2026-05-07), this decision is real and unchanged in shape; engagement timing is gated on the licence-application clock starting, which itself is gated on substrate-complete (the new pre-licence go-live readiness gate).

options.label: Engage now
options.description: Engage a partner firm immediately.
options.consequence: Earliest start; some retainer cost during pre-application phase; firm becomes a deep partner ahead of application.

options.label: Engage 6 months pre-lodgment
options.description: Standard timing.
options.consequence: Conventional engagement; firm has time to draft and run regulator meetings; matches Imani's likely recommendation.

options.label: Engage 9 months pre-lodgment
options.description: Conservative timing; firm has full window.
options.consequence: Slightly more cost; full preparation runway.

options.label: No external counsel
options.description: Run application via internal Imani only.
options.consequence: Significantly higher application risk; not market-standard for SA banking licences.

recommendation.stance: Engage 6–9 months ahead of lodgment; let Imani's recommendation paper land first.
recommendation.reasoning: External counsel is essentially required for a credible SARB application. Timing 6–9 months ahead is conventional and well-justified. Decision can wait ~6 months; Imani's recommendation paper can land in the meantime.

brief.summary: Under the AI-driven-bank reframe, the bank's real costs during build are Anthropic API spend and (when M8 cloud lift happens) Azure infrastructure. Marc sets the monthly cap; Camille tracks actuals against it.
brief.background: Real cost lines for the build phase: (1) Anthropic API tokens — billed monthly to Marc's Anthropic account; scales with agent activity, prompt-cache hit rate, and session count; (2) Azure cloud infrastructure — zero today (local Bun + sqlite); real after M8 lift; order-of-magnitude $X00s-$X,000s/month at the substrate scope. No payroll, no insurance, no rent, no professional fees during the build. The decision sets the monthly cap and the trigger for revisiting (e.g. cap hit two months in a row, or Atlas / Anya request budget for a specific build sub-phase).

options.label: Tight cap with monthly review
options.description: Low monthly cap; review every month; expand as needed.
options.consequence: Forces explicit decision each cycle; keeps budget conscious; may slow build.

options.label: Generous cap with quarterly review
options.description: Higher monthly cap; review quarterly.
options.consequence: Less friction; higher absolute spend; lower decision overhead.

options.label: Cap by sub-phase (M-phase aligned)
options.description: Cap derived from Atlas's M-phase cost estimates; reset per M-phase.
options.consequence: Aligns budget to engineering sequence; requires Atlas estimates to land first.

options.label: No formal cap; review on signal
options.description: No pre-agreed cap; review when monthly bill triggers attention.
options.consequence: Lowest overhead; weakest discipline; only suitable while spend is small.

recommendation.stance: Tight cap with monthly review during early build; transition to cap-by-sub-phase as Atlas's M-phase cost estimates land.
recommendation.reasoning: API spend is genuinely small today; monthly review creates the discipline of revisiting cost intentionally rather than letting it drift. As substrate work scopes up, M-phase-aligned caps give engineering predictability.

brief.summary: Build phase ends at the pre-licence go-live readiness gate (substrate-complete). Atlas + Anya draft a substrate-completeness budget: how many agent runs / sessions of focused engineering work are needed to reach the gate, broken down by domain.
brief.background: Under Principle 7 + the AI-driven-bank reframe, build-phase duration is measured in agent runs and Marc's session cadence, not weeks. Atlas + Anya's spec at `Owner Inbox/2026-05-07_atlas_agent-runtime-substrate-spec.md` is the input. The decision approves a scope-vs-quality tradeoff: e.g. minimum-viable substrate (event runtime + scheduler + recon harnesses) is X sessions; production-grade substrate (with full Vera audit-pipeline coverage and projection persistence) is X+Y sessions.

options.label: Minimum-viable substrate
options.description: Smallest substrate that can run agents autonomously between sessions; defer projection persistence, ML platform, advanced detection.
options.consequence: Earlier licence-application; more substrate gaps to close at licence-day.

options.label: Production-grade substrate
options.description: Full substrate including projection persistence, ML platform, advanced detection, full Vera audit pipelines.
options.consequence: Longer build phase; cleaner licence-application posture.

options.label: Phase-gated (minimum then production)
options.description: Hit minimum-viable first; reassess at that gate before extending to production-grade.
options.consequence: Optionality preserved; mid-phase decision required.

recommendation.stance: Phase-gated (minimum then production).
recommendation.reasoning: Reaching minimum-viable proves the model works; the reassessment gate is the right place to decide whether to extend or push to licence-application directly. Avoids upfront over-commitment.

recommendation.stance: Approve with named cuts: defer ML platform; defer advanced detection (deception, UBA); land minimum-viable runtime first.
recommendation.reasoning: Minimum-viable runtime is the binding constraint on every persona; the deferred items are not (Senna can keep operating against synthetic flows). Phase-gated approach is consistent with S7's recommended stance.

openDecisionsOwned.owner: Imani

brief.summary: Major-firm external counsel is conventionally engaged 6–9 months ahead of SARB licence application. Imani recommends 2–3 firms with strengths-and-weaknesses notes.
brief.background:
Imani is the internal legal-as-code engineer; she runs ECTA execution, master-agreement-as-code, clause libraries, and the legal-entity tree. SARB licence applications conventionally engage a major-firm partner alongside internal counsel for: application drafting (long-form regulatory submissions), regulator engagement and meetings, licence-condition negotiation, and post-grant licence-condition compliance setup. Engagement timing is typically 6–9 months ahead of lodgment. Indicative licence lodgment from today is 12–18 months out, so the engagement decision can wait ~6 months but Imani's recommendation paper can land ahead of the engagement decision.

Under the AI-driven-bank reframe (2026-05-07), this decision is real and unchanged in shape; engagement timing is gated on the licence-application clock starting, which itself is gated on substrate-complete (the new pre-licence go-live readiness gate).

options.label: Engage now
options.description: Engage a partner firm immediately.
options.consequence: Earliest start; some retainer cost during pre-application phase; firm becomes a deep partner ahead of application.

options.label: Engage 6 months pre-lodgment
options.description: Standard timing.
options.consequence: Conventional engagement; firm has time to draft and run regulator meetings; matches Imani's likely recommendation.

options.label: Engage 9 months pre-lodgment
options.description: Conservative timing; firm has full window.
options.consequence: Slightly more cost; full preparation runway.

options.label: No external counsel
options.description: Run application via internal Imani only.
options.consequence: Significantly higher application risk; not market-standard for SA banking licences.

recommendation.stance: Engage 6–9 months ahead of lodgment; let Imani's recommendation paper land first.
recommendation.reasoning: External counsel is essentially required for a credible SARB application. Timing 6–9 months ahead is conventional and well-justified. Decision can wait ~6 months; Imani's recommendation paper can land in the meantime.

openDecisionsOwned.owner: Owen

brief.summary: Banks Act + Companies Act + FIC + POPIA + FAIS together require a thin layer of real humans at licence-day. Owen drafts the composition (which seats, which humans, what cadence) for CEO approval. Replaces the prior 'when to start NED search' framing under the AI-driven-bank reframe.
brief.background: Under the AI-driven-bank operating model (2026-05-07), the bank's labour force is autonomous AI agents. Statutory humans are kept to the minimum the law requires. Realistically 5-10 humans at licence-day: Board exec + NEDs (Companies Act + Banks Act), CEO (Marc), MLRO + FIC Compliance Officer (FIC s.43A / s.43B), Information Officer (POPIA s.56), Auditor (Companies Act s.90 + Banks Act), and FAIS key individuals where Cat II/IIA mandate is sought. Marc currently covers CEO + interim Chair + interim IO + interim MLRO. Owen drafts which seats must have separate humans, candidate sourcing pathway, and timing relative to licence-application.

options.label: Marc covers maximum seats (interim)
options.description: Marc serves as CEO + Chair + IO + MLRO + FIC CO + interim director. NEDs + Auditor are the only additional humans.
options.consequence: Lowest human-headcount; concentrates fit-and-proper risk on Marc; SARB may push back on IO + MLRO concentration.

options.label: Marc + minimum independent layer
options.description: Marc covers CEO. NEDs (2-3) cover Chair + AC chair + RC chair. Separate IO, separate MLRO + FIC CO, separate Auditor.
options.consequence: 5-7 additional humans. SARB-credible; cleaner fit-and-proper distribution.

options.label: Standard SARB-licensed bank composition
options.description: Full Board (Chair + 3-4 NEDs + 1-2 EDs), separate CEO, CRO, CFO, CISO, IO, MLRO, FIC CO, Auditor, FAIS KIs.
options.consequence: 10-15 humans. Highest cost; safest licence-application posture; closest to a conventional bank.

options.label: Defer until SARB engagement
options.description: Hold the decision until external counsel (S5) advises on minimum composition.
options.consequence: Owen drafts alternatives; decision reopens after counsel engagement.

recommendation.stance: Marc + minimum independent layer.
recommendation.reasoning: SARB licence-application credibility requires independent IO and independent MLRO; Marc covering all four roles (CEO + IO + MLRO + Chair) concentrates fit-and-proper exposure and weakens the application. NEDs are required by Banks Act regardless. Going beyond the minimum independent layer is premature before counsel engages.
